fifth_change.decided_by: commit plan rule for live-found functional defects
fifth_change.reason: P3-A live attempt aborted BEFORE any mutation: the delete dialog refused with the probe-unavailable message and no preview/approval was ever offered; nothing was deleted (owner-confirmed). Root finding of this commit: the probe channel collapsed three distinct failure stages (process not authorized, event not resolvable, probe emission unparseable) into one stageless null — same diagnosis-defect class as the 422-without-reason live finding. The repair adds the typed failure stage through Tauri command, transport and dialog, plus the previously missing contract pin for the real ObjC JSON emission parsing into the Rust probe (the fakes had injected structs and never exercised that leg). No eligibility loosening, no delete path without a fresh native probe, architecture untouched. The actual failing stage is determined by the next owner-run attempt; further repair follows the then-proven stage.

sixth_change.decided_by: commit plan rule for live-found functional defects
sixth_change.reason: Owner-run diagnosis attempt returned the typed stage probe_unparseable, excluding TCC and identifier resolution. Observed (not derived, R6) at the same clang/SDK with the same expression forms: clang boxes bare comparison expressions in @() as 0/1 NUMBERS while BOOL-typed expressions box as true/false; exactly the four probe truth values built from comparisons therefore fell fail-closed at the Rust contract. The shim is the wrong side (the probe contract demands truth values; the parser stays strict). Repair: BOOL-typed locals for the four fields; the broken emission is pinned as a must-fail regression; a source guard forbids boxing comparison/logic expressions in the write shim; the probe_unparseable stage now carries the raw emission (PII-poor by construction) so any future drift is observed, never guessed. The prior parse pin was green because it pinned the derived assumption on both sides instead of the observed emission — recorded as the actual finding.

split_justification.context_rule: If the context runs short, work stops before the commit and reports, rather than leaving finished work unsecured or committing it unverified.
split_justification.reason: The owner's staged acceptance (create, halt, update, halt, delete, halt) maps to one stable functional commit per stage; a live-found functional defect creates a further functional commit with a machine-readable reason here, never an amend. The governance position exists because no decision may enter a normative commit before its id is reserved, and the mutation path may not exist before the write decision is codified.
split_justification.separation: normative and determinative stay separate; positions 2-4 are the staged functional verticals create/update/delete, each carried to its live result with an owner halt before the next
